name: Julian Oh
life: “I used to paint fake whiskers on packages with badly printed faces.” People around the downtown fountain know Julian by a small Tuesday habit. Julian keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I drew a moustache on the author. Decades later my granddaughter guessed it was me from the shape.
appearance: Julian is easy to recognize by tightly curled gray hair and a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones. Usually dressed in a dark green knitted vest with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial, Julian raises one eyebrow long before saying yes when listening.
personality: Julian talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Julian's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To give the granddaughter the original mustache drawing.
family: Remy Knight is Julian’s first cousin once removed. When a family elder realized nobody could pronounce a friend's original name, she spent a whole evening teaching the table the three difficult sounds. Under pressure the family still says the names slowly. Julian will correct a mistake even if it makes a meal awkward. Asked about *The new language at dinner*, Remy says, “I hold the client's hand at meals. Yesterday he said my name correctly in a language I have never spoken.”
connections: Lina King. The missing chapter and the penciled mustache finally find their way into the same conversation. Also in the story is Bess Lai (fellow margin writer).

reactions.situation: Two people remember writing the same line
reactions.response: Julian lets both readers identify the line privately before adding a name.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Julian says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
